merger_description:
Motorola Solutions, Inc. (**MSI**), through its subsidiary Motorola Solutions Finance EMEA Limited (**MSF EMEA**), proposes to acquire all of the issued and outstanding shares of D-Fend Solutions AD Ltd. (**D-Fend Solutions**) (the **Acquisition**). Upon completion, D-Fend Solutions will become a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of MSI.

MSI is a US‑domiciled company that supplies mission‑critical communications, video security and access control, and command centre software products and solutions for public safety, government (including defence), and enterprise customers. MSF EMEA is the holding entity for MSI's operating subsidiaries in the UK, EU, Israel, and Norway.

D‑Fend Solutions is an Israel‑based technology company specialising in counter‑unmanned aircraft system (C‑UAS) technology. D‑Fend Solutions supplies devices that detect, identify and mitigate unauthorised drones, including through radio frequency, radar and optical detection technologies. Its products are supplied primarily to public safety and critical infrastructure customers.

events.title: Motorola Solutions - D-Fend Solutions - Phase 1 determination
events.determination_commission_division: Determination made by Commissioner Williams pursuant to a delegation under section 25(1) of the Act

determination_table_content.details:
Motorola Solutions, Inc. (MSI), through its subsidiary Motorola
Solutions Finance EMEA Limited (MSF EMEA), proposes to acquire
all of the issued and outstanding shares of D-Fend Solutions AD Ltd.
(D-Fend Solutions) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, MSF EMEA. is the holding entity for MSI's operating
subsidiaries in the UK, EU, Israel, and Norway.
MSI is a US-domiciled company that supplies mission-critical
communications, video security and access control, and command
centre software products and solutions for public safety,
government (including defence), and enterprise customers.
The target, D-Fend Solutions, is an Israel-based technology company
specialising in counter-unmanned aircraft system (C-UAS)
technology. D-Fend Solutions supplies devices that detect, identify
and mitigate unauthorised drones, including through radio
frequency, radar and optical detection technologies. Its products are
supplied primarily to public safety and critical infrastructure
customers.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the Parties
determination_table_content.details:
There are no horizontal overlaps or vertical relationships between
MSI (and its connected entities) and D-Fend Solutions in Australia.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• There are no horizontal overlaps or vertical relationships
between MSI and D-Fend Solutions.
• The merged entity would be unlikely to have the ability or
incentive to engage in anti-competitive bundling or tying.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
